@graph.headline: Maximum Drawdown in Trading: How to Calculate It, What It Hides, and Whether You Can Survive It

acceptedAnswer.text: The largest peak-to-trough decline in account equity over a period, measured from the running peak (high-water mark) before a new peak is reached. MDD = (Peak − Trough) ÷ Peak × 100. The defining point: it is measured from the peak, not from your starting balance.

mainEntity.name: What is maximum drawdown in trading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Build the equity curve, mark each running peak, measure every decline to the trough before the next new high, convert each to a percentage of that peak, and keep the worst. The ₹ worked example earlier in this article walks through the full calculation, including the percent-vs-rupees trap.

mainEntity.name: How do you calculate maximum drawdown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because once equity climbs above the original balance, the next drawdown measures against the new high-water mark — the risk you actually felt. Using the starting balance understates risk after a strong run (a 20% fall from a peak can still show as a "gain" from the start) and makes two traders with identical P&L report misleadingly different risk from curve shape alone.

mainEntity.name: Why is maximum drawdown measured from the peak, not from where you started?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 10–20% band is the sanity range for active retail strategies: below 10% for intraday F&O, 20–30% accepted for swing trading with multi-day exposure. Beyond 20%, both the recovery math and decision quality degrade — but that 20% line is a guideline, a decision-quality threshold, not a hard rule.

mainEntity.name: What is a good maximum drawdown for a retail trader?

acceptedAnswer.text: The recovery asymmetry: a 50% fall needs +100% to come back, a gain compounded on a halved base. Beyond the math, deep drawdowns degrade decision quality — the strain starts rewriting your rules before the numbers recover. The full recovery mathematics is covered in Trading Drawdown: The Mathematics of Recovery.

mainEntity.name: Why is a 50% drawdown so dangerous?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drawdown is any temporary dip from a peak — the ordinary weather of trading. Maximum drawdown is the largest such decline over the period: the historical worst case, the deepest pain the strategy endured. It also gives you a baseline: if a current drawdown exceeds the strategy's historical maximum, that is an evidence-based signal something may have changed — though MDD alone cannot diagnose a live system in real time.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between drawdown and max drawdown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three things it hides: frequency (one 25% drawdown vs five 20% ones — same headline, different life), duration underwater (how long recovery to a new high took), and sample luck (the recorded worst is the floor of the possible worst, never the ceiling). MDD without these three is a trophy number, not a decision input.

mainEntity.name: What does maximum drawdown NOT tell you?

acceptedAnswer.text: As a live breach line, not a descriptive stat: static vs trailing floors, balance vs equity bases, end-of-day vs intraday recalculation. Cross it in real time and the account ends. For self-funded retail traders, the right takeaway is short: borrow the discipline, not the rules.
